findings.dimension: exact-cut certification (base-physics unreachability of T with conserved-invariant justification)
findings.claim_under_test: In proof_world(13) (p=13, nreg=3, 2197 states), T=(0,1,7) is unreachable from S=(0,0,0) under base physics {inc_r, dec_r, rst_r, dbl_r, neg_r} by any path of any length, justified by the conserved linear invariant f(v)=v[2].
findings.attack_performed: (1) Re-implemented all 5 base ops from scratch (bypassing the project's run_micro interpreter) and ran an independent BFS transitive closure from S over the 2197-state space. (2) Exhaustively verified f(v)=v[2] conservation for every base op on every one of the 2197 states, plus an exhaustive search over all 2196 nonzero linear functionals mod 13 for conserved invariants. (3) Cross-checked their run_micro interpreter against my independent semantics on all 2197x5 op applications, verified base_ops membership, states() enumeration (2197 unique), and the world fingerprint against d7_report.json. (4) Tried to reach T with 20,000 random base-op walks of 60 steps each. (5) Verified the closed-form argument that every base op fixes coords (u,s) on every state, making the cut exact for unbounded path lengths.
findings.evidence: Independent BFS closure from S: exactly 13 states, all of form (r,0,0), r=0..12; T=(0,1,7) not in closure — matches report reachable_count=13 / state_space=2197. Invariant f(v)=v[2]: 0 violations over 2197 states x 5 ops; f(S)=0, f(T)=7. Exhaustive invariant search: 168 conserved functionals (all with weight 0 on r), matching report invariant_count=168; witness (0,0,1) confirmed. Interpreter cross-check: 0 mismatches over 2197x5 applications. world.fingerprint()=381138f433643e36e544b4e7c44f903e8cfa010b164d006fa78a421ec0c12f91 matches report. Every base op fixes (u,s) on every state (True over all 2197x5), so any composition preserves u=0,s=0 from S while T needs u=1,s=7 — cut holds for any path length. Random-walk attack: 0 hits in 20,000 walks x 60 steps. Bonus: f(v)=v[1] also conserved and also separates S from T.
findings.notes: The cut is doubly certified: exact finite-space transitive closure plus an algebraic invariant, and both were reproduced fully independently of the author's certify.py and interpreter. Cosmetic only: stale docstring in substrate.py line 6 says "for the proof world nreg=2" but actual nreg=3; no bearing on the claim.

findings.dimension: controls: base-macro replay and edge reweighting cannot cross the certified cut
findings.claim_under_test: The S->T crossing (S=(0,0,0), T=(0,1,7) in W-PROOF(p=13)) is NOT reproducible by reweighting base edges or by compiling/replaying base-op macros; controls.reweight_navigator and controls.macro_replay both return crossed=False.
findings.attack_performed: Re-derived everything without trusting the report. (1) Verified the deployed world (altworlds.proof_kit(13)) matches worlds.proof_world: 5 base ops (inc_r/dec_r/rst_r/dbl_r/neg_r), fingerprint 381138f4... equal to report's world_fp. (2) Built an INDEPENDENT semantic model of the 5 base ops and cross-checked it against substrate.run_micro on all 2197 states x 5 ops. (3) Computed base closure from S with my own BFS + my own arithmetic (reweighting invariance: no new edges, so reachable set is this closure). (4) Strong random macro attack: 5000 random base-op sequences of length 1-12 per seed, 5 seeds, BFS closure under base+macros from S, checked for T. Also reran author's macro_replay with harder settings (2000 macros, max_len=12, seed=99). (5) EXHAUSTIVE upgrade beyond the requested length-12 search: computed the full transformation monoid generated by the base ops (closure of function tables under composition), covering every base-op macro of ANY length, and checked whether any element reaches T from S or moves registers u,s on any state.
findings.evidence: Interpreter-vs-independent-model mismatches over all 2197x5 base-op applications: 0; base ops violating (u,s)-conservation: 0. Independent base closure from S: 13 states, all of form (r,0,0), T=(0,1,7) NOT in closure — so reweighting E0 (which adds no transitions) cannot cross. Random macro attack (5000 macros, len<=12), seeds 0-4: reachable=13, crossed=False every seed. Exhaustive monoid of ALL base-op sequences: 169 distinct functions; states reachable from S under any of them: 13; T reachable: False; monoid elements moving u or s on any state: 0 — proving no base macro of ANY length (not just <=12) can cross. Author controls reproduce: reweight_navigator -> {crossed: False, reachable: 13}; macro_replay default and hardened (n_macros=2000, max_len=12, seed=99) -> {crossed: False, reachable: 13}; matches d7_report.json controls section. Files: F:/SerendipityB/d7/worlds.py (base = r-only ops, lines 52-56), F:/SerendipityB/d7/controls.py (lines 26-63), F:/SerendipityB/d7/certify.py (base_closure), F:/SerendipityB/d7/run.py (lines 207-211).
findings.notes: The soundness is structural, not sampling luck: all five base ops are single-instruction programs writing only register 0 (addk/subk/set/mulk on reg 0), so registers u=reg1 and s=reg2 are conserved exactly by every base op, hence by every composition; the monoid computation makes this exhaustive for unbounded macro length. Any T with u=1,s=7 is therefore unreachable via base macros or reweighting. The only s-writer (spush) and u-writer (uset) live in the hoard, not base physics. Controls' reweight_navigator ignores its budget/seed args and just computes base closure — a fair implementation, since reweighting a fixed edge set provably cannot change the reachable set.

findings.dimension: nonlinearity/context-dependence of admitted z and correctness of degeneracy classifier
findings.claim_under_test: The admitted z is genuinely nonlinear/context-dependent (not affine, not coordinate-separable) and controls.classify_degeneracy correctly flags degenerate (affine/separable) cases.
findings.attack_performed: Independently re-ran the H2 search (H2 prior re-derived from generate_history+derive_prior; evo search, primary pair (0,0,0)->(0,1,7), seeds 0-7, budget 1500) and recovered the admitted z byte-identical to the report: seq(spush_dup, seq(seq(uset, spush), rep4(rep4(step_dup)))). Materialized z:V->V myself over all 2197 states with my own loop and fault policy (0 faults). Attacked affinity two ways: (a) forced-candidate check — any affine Av+b is uniquely determined by z(0) and z(e_i), verified against all 2197 states; (b) additivity of g(v)=z(v)-z(0) as a necessary condition for ANY affine map. Attacked separability with a test strictly stronger than the classifier's: for each output coord, checked dependence on each single input coord (all 9 pairs), i.e. permuted/generalized separability, not just same-index. Counted distinct deltas z(v)-v for context dependence and tabulated z((r,0,0)) vs z((r,1,0)). Then built truly degenerate z's — ungated s+=r (affine), r+=1 (affine+separable), r+=r*r (separable but nonlinear), and an affine composite seq(s+=r, rep3(r+=1)) — and ran controls.classify_degeneracy on each.
findings.evidence: Re-derived z identical to reported: True; H2 solved 8/8 seeds (first-solve evals 20,4,3,114,9,27,49,44). NOT AFFINE: forced candidate b=z(0)=(3,1,0), A cols [(1,0,1),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)] mismatches 1859/2197 states (e.g. v=(2,0,0): z(v)=(5,1,4) vs pred (5,1,2)); additivity counterexample g((1,0,0))+g((1,0,0))=(2,0,2) != g((2,0,0))=(2,0,4) rules out every affine A,b. NOT SEPARABLE: output coord 2 depends on no single input coord (candidates: coord0->[0], coord1->[1], coord2->[]), so not even permuted-separable. CONTEXT-DEPENDENT: 13 distinct deltas z(v)-v; s-output is r^2 from u=0 inputs vs 2r^2 from u=1 inputs (r=2: s=4 vs 8; r=4: 3 vs 6; r=5: 12 vs 11). Classifier on planted degenerates: ungated s+=r -> affine=True DEGENERATE_LINEAR; r+=1 -> affine=True sep=True DEGENERATE_LINEAR; r+=r*r -> affine=False sep=True DEGENERATE_LINEAR; affine composite -> DEGENERATE_LINEAR. Classifier on admitted z: all four degeneracy tests False, nonlinear_gate_pass=True. Cut barrier True, z crosses True, T not in base closure.
findings.notes: _affine_fit (F:/SerendipityB/d7/controls.py) is mathematically complete: an affine fit is forced by images of 0 and the unit vectors, then verified over the full state space. One latent (non-triggered) weakness: _coordinate_separable only tests same-index dependence, so a nonlinear permuted-separable map (e.g. swap-then-square) could in principle evade the degeneracy gate; the admitted z fails even the generalized permuted test, so this gap cannot affect the current verdict.

findings.dimension: relational-advantage-fairness (H2 vs history-free baselines; arm symmetry)
findings.claim_under_test: H2 finds a crossing ~3x faster than the strongest history-free baseline and ~2.8x faster than H0; Z0/Z1 differ only in the proposal prior art_w (same grammar, hoard, verifier, budget, shaping fitness)
findings.attack_performed: (1) Audited evalz.py/search.py/run.py for history or per-artifact identity in the fitness/verifier path; grep of evalz.py for store/history/art_w/label/role terms found none. (2) Runtime identity-blindness proof: permuted all artifact ids and re-evaluated 201 programs incl. the reported primary z — 0 mismatches in best_dist/closure_size/reached. (3) Independently re-derived H0/H1/H2 priors from a fresh generate_history run and inspected which artifacts get weight. (4) Re-ran uniform-sample, uniform-evo, H0, H1, H2 on the primary pair (6 seeds, budget 1000). (5) Adversarial concentration-only control: same weight multiset {12,12,8,8} on 4 random artifacts, 6 trials, to test whether mere prior concentration explains the speedup.
findings.evidence: Re-run medians (primary pair, seeds 0-5, budget 1000): H2=14.5, uniform-sample=33, uniform-evo=33, H0=58.5, H1=87 -> H2 2.28x vs strongest history-free, 4.03x vs H0, 6.0x vs H1 (report's full 6-pairs x 8-seeds matrix: 3.11x, 2.79x, 3.66x). Priors: H2 upweights exactly {uset,uset_dup,spush,spush_dup}=12/12/8/8; H0 only {uset,uset_dup}=5/5 (spush marginally invisible: inert solo since probes pin u=0); H1 has MORE total mass (89 vs 68) on 8 mostly-wrong artifacts, so the edge is not prior mass. Concentration-only control: {12,12,8,8} on random artifact quadruples gives medians 236, 253.5, 306, 500.5, 152, 500.5 — all far worse than uniform (33), so concentrated weighting alone HURTS; the speedup requires the relationally-correct wiring. Identity-relabel test: 201 programs, 0 mismatches — fitness is a pure function of behavior, not artifact identity. evalz.py grep for store|history|art_w|label|role: no matches.
findings.notes: Minor caveats, none rising to a defect: (a) my primary-pair-only rerun gives 2.28x vs strongest history-free rather than ~3x; the reported 3.11x comes from the full 48-unit matrix (n=6 here is noisy; direction and materiality confirmed). (b) 'Z0/Z1 differ only in art_w' strictly holds for the evo-mode contrasts (H2 vs Z0-evo/H0/H1); Z0-sample/cost/novelty also differ in selection mode as search.py documents, but using the strongest such variant as comparator is conservative against H2. (c) H2's spush upweight flows solely through the pairwise emergent record (marginals show spush touches nothing), which is precisely the claimed relational-history causal channel; H0 with identical marginals lacks it and is ~4x slower. findings.dimension: irreducible-compositionality of barrier crossing (no single-artifact opener)
findings.claim_under_test: No single hoard artifact and no size-<=2 program crosses the barrier; crossing requires composing >=2 distinct artifacts (uset gate-writer + gated nonlinear spush); census density ~0.0036 with no KILL flags.
findings.attack_performed: Built hoard.build_hoard(13) and re-derived everything with evalz.evaluate: (a) net-effect audit of all 32 artifacts over the full 2197-state space to hunt hidden u/s writers; (b) exhaustive test of all 32 single quotes plus rep(n,quote) n=1..20 and ifz(c,quote) c=0..2 against all 6 family targets; (c) exhaustive test of all 32x32=1024 ordered seq(quote,quote) pairs; (d) 5000 random ASTs per artifact restricted to a single distinct artifact id (max_nodes=16, rep/ifz on); (e) two independent census re-runs with my own seeds (12345, 999; n=4000) plus a 6000-sample crosser autopsy verifying every crosser quotes both a uset* and a spush*.
findings.evidence: Singles: 0 crossers (quotes, rep n=1..20, ifz c=0..2). Pairs: exactly 8/1024 cross, precisely {a00 spush, a13 spush_dup} x {a22 uset_dup, a26 uset} in both orders; same-artifact pairs never cross. Register audit: only a26/a22 net-write u, only a00/a13 net-write s; other 28 artifacts r-only or identity. Single-distinct-artifact hunt: 0 crossers in 32x5000 random programs. Independent census: seed=12345 density 0.00475 min_size 3 KILL_FLAGS=[]; seed=999 density 0.0015 min_size 4 KILL_FLAGS=[]; author's 0.00363/min 3/no flags is consistent. Autopsy: 21/21 crossers in my 6000-sample run quote both uset* and spush*; minimal crosser ('seq',('quote','a26'),('quote','a00')) at z_size 3.
findings.notes: Minor doc nit, not a defect of the claim: hoard.py's docstring says only the ORDERED pair (uset then spush) works, but seq(spush,uset) also crosses because the z-macro is applied repeatedly in the Gz closure (u becomes nonzero after the first application, so later spush firings succeed, e.g. u=1 via 14 applications). Crossing still requires exactly the two distinct artifact roles, so the audited claim holds. Report top crosser usage (a13,a26,a22,a00) maps exactly to spush_dup,uset,uset_dup,spush, consistent with my findings. Scripts: scratchpad attack1.py, attack2.py.

(2) Re-certified the xfer cut with my own BFS and my own exhaustive u/s-conservation check (all 4913 states x 5 base ops); tested every single artifact as a lone macro. (3) Re-ran the frozen proof-z verbatim in the xfer world; also tested a role-remapped variant. (4) Re-ran Z0-evo vs Z-MECH on frozen seeds 0-7 (replication) and fresh seeds 100-107 (anti-cherry-pick), plus an adversarial shuffled-prior control (same weight multiset on wrong artifacts, 3 shuffles) to test whether mere prior concentration explains the advantage. Writer semantics verified: proof s+=r^2 mod 13 vs xfer s+=r^3 mod 17 on 12 gate-open probes; target families disjoint. findings.notes: Three non-fatal caveats. (a) Gate check "identity_does_not_transfer" is hardcoded True in altworlds.py:227 — 1 of 5 checks is vacuous; the other four demonstrably catch clones. (b) The headline 15x ratio (116 vs 7.5) is seed-favorable: fresh seeds give ~4x (34.5 vs 8.5); direction and significance are robust but the magnitude is unstable. (c) 14 of 20 xfer artifacts are byte-identical to proof artifacts (p-agnostic neutrals, gate writer, r-ctrl, 4/5 distractors), so the docstring's "distractor inventory differs" is overstated — however the crossing-critical nonlinear writer, modulus, base semantics, and endpoints genuinely differ, and the gate never claims hoard disjointness.
